messages:
maria: Customer reported SSE stream closed mid-response when they put Android phone into pocket. Partial text delivered, app shows completed error. Customer wants repro steps and possible billing credit.

maria: Repro steps they gave: 1) Open convo, 2) trigger streaming response, 3) let tokens stream for ~3-6s, 4) slide phone into pocket — stream closes within ~2-10s with partial output. Happens on both Wifi and 4G for them. Device: Pixel 6a, Android 13, battery saver OFF but "Pocket mode" enabled via vendor.

maria: Attached sanitized logs from client: 
```
[STREAM] started id=abc123
[data] {"chunk":"Hello, here is the start..."}
[STREAM] connection closed: EOF
[HTTP] code=200 -> socket closed by peer
```

sanjay: Thanks, can we get the connection close reason from the proxy logs? Do we see any TLS-level alert or just EOF? Also: is the client sending any keepalive pings?

kate: Mobile-side notes: a few vendors implement aggressive link suspend when pocket/cover sensor triggers. That can tear sockets without notifying app (link-layer power-save). On Android this can look like a fast-RST or silent close. If the app doesn't send periodic application-level keepalive, connection can die mid-stream.

owen: Looking at infra trace for trace_id=trace-20240318-9f7: downstream saw FIN from client side at 1719123468, upstream kept stream open for 1s, no TCP RST from server. Proxy logs: 
```
2024-03-18T12:24:28Z proxy: conn_id=zz-77 downstream FIN received, stream aborted, client_ip=10.2.3.4
```
No TLS alerts. So it looks like client device closed socket (or OS did).

kate: If OS forces a close, mobile should treat SSE close as transient and retry. For streaming completions we currently treat midstream close as final and mark the request failed. We should change client to: 1) detect midstream EOF, 2) surface "incomplete" state to user with option to retry, 3) attempt automatic reconnect & ask server for resume via Last-Event-ID if server supports it.

maria: Customer is upset because they were billed for the partial output. Billing policy clarification requested.

billing-bot: Policy reminder: tokens emitted before server-side completion are billable. However, we can offer credits on a case-by-case for UX regressions. Please include evidence of reproducible device-level behavior if you want a manual credit.

kevin: Assigning to mobile eng to add short-term mitigation: 1) send an SSE comment line every 10s from client as keepalive (or use XHR/WS fallback), 2) show retry UI for midstream close. Long-term: evaluate server-side resume semantics (last-event-id) for chat.

kate: Quick repro I used: adb forward tcp:8080 tcp:8080, start app, then simulate pocket by toggling wifi interface down: `adb shell svc wifi disable` — stream closes after ~3s, same behavior. Workaround on app: call `setKeepAlive(true)` on socket or schedule a 5s noop POST to keep NAT/power alive.

owen: Also see increased 502 counts from some mobile pools when phones rapidly toggle network. Suggest adding an internal metric: sse_midstream_client_close_count by device OS vendor.

maria: Next steps for support: 1) share mobile repro snippet with customer (adb commands + curl reproduction), 2) offer a goodwill credit if customer agrees to test patch, 3) track incident for mobile UX.

sanjay: Technical note: server cannot safely resume arbitrary generation without model state. We could support resumable streams if client sends a deterministic prefix and we re-run generation with same prompt plus prefix as context — but that may re-run compute and complicate billing. For now focus on client-side keepalive + retry UI.

kate: I'll open a mobile ticket (MOB-1123) to implement keepalive+retry and add a small telemetry flag. Will ping when patch available.

maria: Thanks all — passing to customer with repro and suggested mitigations. :thumbsup:
